blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust inside Telecom, Media & Entertainment: what the sector's controls demand, what we build on the platform rails, and the outcomes written into the engagement.

In Telecom, Media & Entertainment, cybersecurity & zero-trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, ai-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (soc 2, iso 27001, pci dss, dora) that regulated industries must evidence. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: zero-trust architecture & implementation, threat intelligence & managed soc, identity & access modernization — delivered on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Signaling and core exposure
SS7/Diameter weaknesses, API exposure and core-estate sprawl create nation-grade threat surfaces; regulator attention is rising.
Network telemetry underused
Element managers, probes and tickets feed separate systems; NOC decisions remain reactive. The estate generates petabytes that never reach a decision model.
Churn saves run on campaign calendars
Retention offers fire in monthly batches; in-quarter intent signals (support tickets, usage drops, billing disputes) do not trigger saves in the moment.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: NIS2 / sector cyber regulation and NERC/sector-specific grid-adjacent rules (where utility-adjacent). Operational compliance for infrastructure roles. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Below is the delivery cadence for this capability — the same pattern on every engagement. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
